property_summary: The supportsInterface function should return true if either the direct match or the inherited supportsInterface is true, but the mutant requires both to be true, causing it to return false for some interface IDs that the correct contract would return true for.

For any interfaceId, M.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must not return false when P.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true; specifically the bug requires both direct and inherited matching, so it fails for interfaceIds where only the inherited ERC165 returns true.

The correct supportsInterface returns true whenever at least one of the direct match or the inherited ERC165 returns true; the buggy mutant returns false when only the inherited ERC165 match is true (i.e., for interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId), so the bug returns false where the correct contract returns true.

For any interface ID, if the correct contract P returns true via supportsInterface (matching either IAccessControl directly or inheriting the true from ERC165), the buggy mutant M must not return false; the mutant's AND logic causes it to return false when the direct match fails but the inherited ERC165 match holds (e.g., for type(IERC165).interfaceId).

For any interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface must return true if the mutant returns true; the bug breaks this because M returns false for interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId while P returns true.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C returns true exactly for the expected IERC165 and IAccessControl interfaces, while the bug returns false for all inputs, violating the ERC-165 support for IAccessControl.
The reference contract must support the IAccessControl interface (returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId), while the mutant returns false for all inputs including that interface.

The reference contract C must return true when supportsInterface is called with type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId, and false for all other interface IDs; the mutant always returns false, violating both required true responses.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true, then that interfaceId must be either type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant violates this by returning false for all, effectively making the rule vacuously true in the reference but still showing a difference on the required true cases.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C never reverts on supportsInterface, but the mutant always reverts because it returns false and the override chain requires super calls to be handled.
The hasRole function must return the membership status for the specific account, but the mutant always returns the membership status of address(0) regardless of the account parameter.

The return value of hasRole(role, account) must equal the return value of hasRole(role, other) when both accounts have the same membership, but the mutant returns the same value for all accounts regardless of their membership.

For any role and any two distinct accounts, if hasRole is true for one account, it must be false for the other when only one is granted the role; the mutant always returns the membership of address(0), so it returns the same value for both accounts.
For any role and any account, hasRole(role, account) must equal the membership of that specific account, but the mutant returns the membership of address(0) regardless of the account parameter.
For any role and any account, hasRole(role, account) must return false until a role is granted to that account, but the mutant returns the membership status of address(0) instead.

The reference getRoleAdmin returns the actual admin role stored for any role, while the buggy version always returns 0x00; thus for any role whose admin is set to a non-zero value, the return values differ.

For any bytes32 role, the admin role returned by getRoleAdmin must match the role required to grant that role via grantRole, i.e., the caller must have that admin role to successfully grant the role, which the bug violates by always returning 0x00.

For any bytes32 role where the admin role has been changed from the default, granting that role requires the caller to hold the real admin role; the bug makes getRoleAdmin always return 0x00, so granting a role with a non-zero admin fails even for the correct admin.

For any role whose admin has been explicitly set to a non-zero value via constructor initialization, the correct contract returns that non-zero admin from getRoleAdmin, while the buggy version always returns 0x00, violating the invariant that the returned admin must equal the admin set for that role.

For any role whose admin has been set to a non-default value, getRoleAdmin must return the role that is actually required to call grantRole successfully; the bug returns 0x00, so grantRole called by an account holding the real admin role will revert.

The getRoleAdmin function must return the stored admin role for any given role, not the hash of the role itself. The bug returns the role's own value instead of the stored admin role, which differs for any role that does not have itself set as its admin.
Renouncing a role must revert when the caller is not the account holder, but the buggy version allows anyone to revoke any role from any account.
